$comment_known_red_own_finding: KNOWN-RED ON ITS OWN EVIDENCE, TRACKED AS CHAOS-3534 -- deliberately NOT part of the CHAOS-3533 class, and removed from it after being wrongly filed there. The distinction matters: CHAOS-3533 is 'a terminating preflight writes a ledger row only for AMBIGUOUS_CANDIDATES, so a not-found terminal cannot evidence itself' -- those cases are EXPECTED to terminate unresolved. This case is expected to PROCEED and commit BOTH subjects exactly, so its empty ledger is downstream of the outcome being wrong, not of the row-writing rule; fixing 3533 would not move it. Measured post-CHAOS-3497 (world digest 2e1e254d..., errored 0): scope_resolution_outcome='unresolved' against allowed=['exact'], and resolution_path absent for reason 'empty-resolution-ledger'. Both named subjects are real -- subjects.json carries subject.bounded-set.web-app-and-api-gateway with members ['meridian/web-app','meridian/api-gateway'], and meridian/web-app commits an exact_match in the SAME run under deg.acr-unavailable-native-usable, deg.source-state.not-applicable, trust.conflicting-evidence and scope.refused-with-grounding. So neither subject is missing; the plural/cohort shape is what fails. That is surprising in production's own terms: subject_preflight.py:471-480 (D2, Amendment TRD v2 line 154, CHAOS-3301) presupposes a cohort question CAN reach 'two distinct exactly-resolved mentions'. This one reaches unresolved with no ledger at all. Do not fold this back into 3533 and do not strip its invariants -- a case admitted to a known-red set on another finding's justification is how such sets start growing. It was also named in advance as the least-defensible call in that run's pre-registration, before the result was known.
